Since completing my first Roy Dotrice listen, I've watched that tube video of him reading the tower of joy excerpt numerous times. I've been going through my second listen, and when I got to the Cersei chapter quoted below, icy fingers danced up my spine. I did a quick searchall on "dreamt an old dream" and found the following:

GOT Eddard X:

He dreamt an old dream, of three knights in white cloaks, and a tower long fallen, and Lyanna in her bed of blood.

AFFC Cersei VIII:

She dreamt an old dream, of three girls in brown cloaks, a wattled crone, and a tent that smelled of death.

ADWD Prologue:

He dreamt an old dream of a hovel by the sea, three dogs whimpering, a woman's tears.

In each, a group of three, a location, a woman, and an element of death.

Character Group of Three Location Woman Death
Eddard three knights in white cloaks a tower long fallen Lyanna bed of blood: Lyanna's
Cersei three girls in brown cloaks a tent [Maggy] smell of death: Cersei's and her children? Melara's?
Varamyr three dogs whimpering a hovel by the sea [Varamyr's Mother] tears: for Bump, Varamyr's brother's

So what's going on here? Is this just RR being poetic, or is there a connection or some kind of significance here? I've been spinning this through my mind, stringing together tacks on a map, and crafting an ornate til-foil helm, but I can't seem to bring my suspicions into focus. Some unspoken possible parallels here:

Cersei was one of the three girls; Varamyr warged one of the three dogs; Eddard warged one of the three knights?

Maggy is a woods witch; there was a woods witch at Bump's funeral; was there a woods witch at the TOJ? What are all these woods witches up to?

Varamyr warged a dog to kill Bump; Cersei may have pushed Melara down the well; did Eddard somehow have a hand in Lyanna's death?

What are everyone's thoughts on this? These share so many elements that are jumbled up and rearranged, classic RR. I feel like there must be some spooky connection here, but that might just be misdirection and I might just be going mad.

Very interesting. I'm inclined to think that it's just a literary pattern that GRRM likes to employ: a group of three phrases in which the first phrase references another group of three.

Could be more than that, but there's so many possibilities if we try to read into it that I think it's more likely just GRRM being poetic.

I am supporting this. GRRM likes to repeat different passages to create literary form. It's really cool though, especially when you think of the significance of the first two dreams. One would think that points to the last example having a higher significance than maybe first expected.

What could that meaning possibly be, I wonder...

I think it's safe to say a lot of things mean something at a lot of things don't in his novels, he clearly reuses similar word structures but not always to link them. That's not to say he never does it on purpose I think it's safe to say a lot of things mean something and a lot of things don't in his novels, he clearly reuses similar word structures but not always for deeper meaning.

What's the difference between malware and a virus? I really don't know sorry.

A virus is a code that spread itself by changing other existing executables. For example, it might change notepad.exe (your widows notepad executable file) so that it will contain some malicious code. You start notepad and by doing so you unknowingly start an infected program.

The programs you're talking about don't do that, they are usually programs that you consciously install (you're probably tricked to do that) or install bundled with other software.

Here is a good article about that.

A lot of "viruses" nowadays are spyware. They monitor your computer and pull information. This takes up processing power which slows your computer. Viruses can also use a bit of your computer's processing power for their own purposes, thus slowing your computer down.

A lot of companies also produce "bloatware" which is just super inefficient programs. Some try to open on startup and hide away in the background. Most of the time you get these by not unchecking some checkbox while installing software you actually want, or they are hidden in the custom install options. These companies/programs know people won't want their products and try to sneak in through other desirable software.
